record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: conjugacy search at high Hirsch length
record.original_question: For infinite polycyclic groups of high Hirsch length, determine whether there are algorithms that solve the conjugacy search problem effectively, and give computational complexity bounds for such algorithms if they exist. The question concerns the high-Hirsch-length regime where existing methods for the conjugacy search problem are not known to apply efficiently.

evidence.quote: The algorithm has been implemented and seems to be efficient for groups of small Hirsch length.
Presently there are no known algorithms for infinite polycyclic groups of high Hirsch length.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series
$$ G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\} $$
with each quotient $G_i / G_{i+1}$ cyclic. The Hirsch length $h(G)$ is the number of indices $i$ for which $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is infinite cyclic; it is an invariant of $G$.

The conjugacy search problem in $G$ is: given elements $u, v \in G$ that are known to be conjugate (i.e., there exists $g \in G$ with $g^{-1} u g = v$), produce such an element $g$.

The problem is the following: for infinite polycyclic groups $G$ of arbitrarily large Hirsch length, given by a polycyclic presentation, does there exist an algorithm that solves the conjugacy search problem and runs in time bounded by a stated complexity function (e.g., polynomial in the input size and the Hirsch length)? Either exhibit such an algorithm together with explicit complexity bounds, or prove that no such efficient algorithm can exist (e.g., under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in the regime of high Hirsch length. Known algorithms (e.g., Eick–Kahrobaei) have been implemented and work for small Hirsch length, but no efficient algorithm is known for large Hirsch length. There are families of polycyclic groups for which the uniform conjugacy problem is shown to be NP-complete (Hofheinz–Steinwandt-type constructions, and the arXiv:1403.4153 family), suggesting that no efficient algorithm exists in general; however a definitive resolution—either a worst-case efficient algorithm for arbitrary polycyclic groups, or a matching hardness result for the search version in the natural cryptographic setting—has not been established.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polycyclic groups whose conjugacy problem is at least as hard as subset sum, hence NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: There exist polycyclic groups for which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete, indicating no general efficient algorithm is expected.

status_evidence.title: Length-based attacks in polycyclic groups
status_evidence.snippet: Success rate of length-based attack decreases as Hirsch length increases; high Hirsch length polycyclic groups appear resistant.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental evidence that conjugacy search is hard at high Hirsch length, no efficient algorithm known.

status_evidence.title: Solving the conjugacy decision problem via machine learning
status_evidence.snippet: For a group with Hirsch length 14, the average time of the conjugacy algorithm was over 100 hours.
status_evidence.claim: Existing exact algorithms become impractical for moderate-to-high Hirsch length.
